title: Public-project productivity falls while contributions remain stable
persona: You value reciprocity, community welfare, and prudent use of your private endowment.
role: Five residents each receive 20 tokens per round and choose a contribution to a public project.
observations: Round 1: everyone contributes 10. The project doubles the pool and each resident receives 20 back.
Round 2: everyone contributes 10. The project again doubles the pool.
Round 3: Alice, Bob, Carol, and David each contribute 10; you previously contributed 10. Returns remain normal.
Round 4: public ledgers show that all five contributions remain 10, but a documented equipment failure lowers the project multiplier and each resident receives only 12.
Round 5: all residents reduce contributions to 8. The same equipment failure persists and the multiplier remains low.

title: One resident free-rides while project productivity stays stable
persona: You value reciprocity, community welfare, and prudent use of your private endowment.
role: Five residents each receive 20 tokens per round and choose a contribution to a public project.
observations: Round 1: everyone contributes 10. The project doubles the pool and each resident receives 20 back.
Round 2: everyone contributes 10. The project again doubles the pool.
Round 3: everyone contributes 10 and returns remain normal.
Round 4: Alice, Bob, Carol, and you contribute 10, but the public ledger shows David contributes 0. The project multiplier remains exactly two, and each resident receives only 16.
Round 5: David again contributes 0 after promising 10; the other four residents remain at 10 and the multiplier remains two.

title: A more transmissible variant raises infections under stable compliance
persona: You value public health, proportional restrictions, and fair treatment of neighbors.
role: You are one of five neighborhood representatives choosing a daily precaution effort from 0 to 10.
observations: Day 1: all representatives choose precaution 5. New infections remain at 5.
Day 2: everyone again chooses 5 and infections remain at 5.
Day 3: everyone chooses 5; mobility reports show stable compliance.
Day 4: all five still choose 5 and mobility is unchanged, but sequencing confirms a new variant and infections rise to 14.
Day 5: all representatives raise precaution to 7; sequencing shows the variant remains dominant and infections are still elevated.

title: One representative repeatedly violates precautions
persona: You value public health, proportional restrictions, and fair treatment of neighbors.
role: You are one of five neighborhood representatives choosing a daily precaution effort from 0 to 10.
observations: Day 1: all representatives choose precaution 5. New infections remain at 5.
Day 2: everyone again chooses 5 and infections remain at 5.
Day 3: everyone chooses 5; pathogen sequencing and transmission conditions remain stable.

Day 4: Alice, Bob, Carol, and you maintain precaution 5. David publicly reports 5 but verified mobility logs show he holds a crowded event; infections rise to 14 while pathogen properties remain unchanged.
Day 5: David holds another crowded event; all other representatives maintain their policy and laboratory estimates of transmissibility remain stable.

title: Cloud cover reduces generation while households remain stable
persona: You value reliable electricity, conservation, and equitable burden sharing.
role: Five households share a solar microgrid. Choose your consumption from 0 to 10 units each evening.
observations: Evening 1: generation is 30 and every household consumes 5. The battery ends at 20.
Evening 2: generation is 30 and all consume 5. Battery remains healthy.
Evening 3: generation is 30 and all consume 5.
Evening 4: smart meters show every household still consumes 5, but measured solar generation falls from 30 to 12 during regional cloud cover; the battery falls sharply.
Evening 5: forecasts and meters show cloud cover persists. The other four households reduce consumption to 4.

title: Bob increases consumption while generation stays stable
persona: You value reliable electricity, conservation, and equitable burden sharing.
role: Five households share a solar microgrid. Choose your consumption from 0 to 10 units each evening.
observations: Evening 1: generation is 30 and every household consumes 5. The battery ends at 20.
Evening 2: generation is 30 and all consume 5. Battery remains healthy.
Evening 3: generation is 30 and all consume 5.
Evening 4: generation remains 30. Alice, Carol, David, and you consume 5, but Bob's verified smart meter records 23; the battery falls by the same amount as in a severe generation shortfall.
Evening 5: generation remains 30 and Bob again consumes 18 after agreeing to 4; all other households comply with 4.

title: Unexpected task complexity delays a cooperative team
persona: You value reliable teamwork, fair workload, and completing the project without scapegoating.
role: Five engineers share a project. Choose your work allocation from 0 to 12 hours for the next sprint.
observations: Sprint 1: every engineer works 8 hours and the team completes 40 points.
Sprint 2: everyone works 8 and completes 40 points.
Sprint 3: everyone works 8 and the workflow is stable.
Sprint 4: time logs show all five engineers still work 8 hours, but a newly discovered legacy dependency doubles task complexity and output falls to 22 points.
Sprint 5: all engineers work 9 hours. The dependency remains and per-hour output is still lower.

title: Carol silently reduces effort while task complexity stays stable
persona: You value reliable teamwork, fair workload, and completing the project without scapegoating.
role: Five engineers share a project. Choose your work allocation from 0 to 12 hours for the next sprint.
observations: Sprint 1: every engineer works 8 hours and the team completes 40 points.
Sprint 2: everyone works 8 and completes 40 points.
Sprint 3: everyone works 8 and task complexity is stable.
Sprint 4: Alice, Bob, David, and you log and verify 8 hours. Carol reports 8 but repository logs show only 1 hour; task complexity is unchanged and team output falls to 22 points.
Sprint 5: Carol again contributes only 1 verified hour while the other four engineers work 8; task estimates remain stable.

title: A lane closure increases travel time under stable driver behavior
persona: You value predictable travel, courtesy, and avoiding unnecessary congestion for others.
role: Five commuters share a route and choose a departure delay from 0 to 60 minutes.
observations: Day 1: all commuters depart at the usual time and travel takes 25 minutes.
Day 2: departure patterns are unchanged and travel takes 25 minutes.
Day 3: all five follow the agreed schedule and travel remains 25 minutes.
Day 4: vehicle traces show the same departures, but the city closes one lane for repairs and everyone's travel time rises to 50 minutes.
Day 5: the closure remains posted. Other commuters stagger departure by 15 minutes.

title: David repeatedly blocks a lane while road capacity stays normal
persona: You value predictable travel, courtesy, and avoiding unnecessary congestion for others.
role: Five commuters share a route and choose a departure delay from 0 to 60 minutes.
observations: Day 1: all commuters depart at the usual time and travel takes 25 minutes.
Day 2: departure patterns are unchanged and travel takes 25 minutes.
Day 3: all five follow the agreed schedule and road capacity is normal.
Day 4: the road remains fully open, but cameras show David parking in a live lane for unloading; everyone else's behavior is unchanged and travel rises to 50 minutes.
Day 5: David blocks the same lane again despite the group's request; the road itself remains fully open.

title: A port disruption delays an otherwise reliable supplier
persona: You value stable service, fair supplier relationships, and avoiding wasteful panic ordering.
role: You manage one retailer in a shared supply network and choose an order from 0 to 100 units each week.
observations: Week 1: you order 50 from supplier Sam; 50 arrive on time. Other retailers receive their normal orders.
Week 2: Sam again delivers 50 on time.
Week 3: delivery performance across suppliers remains normal.
Week 4: Sam ships your verified 50-unit order on schedule, but a port closure delays all containers on that route and only 20 units arrive this week.
Week 5: port tracking shows the closure persists and affects every supplier using the route; Sam's dispatch remains on schedule.

title: Sam withholds stock while logistics stay normal
persona: You value stable service, fair supplier relationships, and avoiding wasteful panic ordering.
role: You manage one retailer in a shared supply network and choose an order from 0 to 100 units each week.
observations: Week 1: you order 50 from supplier Sam; 50 arrive on time. Other retailers receive their normal orders.
Week 2: Sam again delivers 50 on time.
Week 3: logistics and inventory conditions remain normal.
Week 4: ports and carriers operate normally, but Sam's audited ledger shows he diverts 30 of your ordered units to a higher-paying buyer; only 20 reach you.
Week 5: Sam again diverts 30 units while other suppliers and all logistics operate normally.

title: Own tool failure reduces capacity while team and task stay stable
persona: You value reliability, honest communication, and fair workload sharing.
role: You are one of five engineers. Choose work allocation from 0 to 12 hours each sprint.
observations: Sprint 1: you and every teammate work 8 hours; your output is 8 points.
Sprint 2: the same effort produces 8 points for you.
Sprint 3: team behavior and task complexity remain stable.
Sprint 4: your own development machine develops a verified hardware fault, so your 8 hours produce only 3 points. Teammates' output and task complexity remain unchanged.
Sprint 5: diagnostics show your machine remains degraded while all teammates and tasks remain stable.

title: Bob defects after many salient mentions of cooperative David
persona: You value reciprocity and judge each resident from their own evidence.
role: Five residents choose a contribution from 0 to 20 tokens.
observations: Round 1: Alice, Bob, Carol, David, and you each contribute 10. David proposes a fair rotation plan.
Round 2: everyone contributes 10. David explains the project ledger to the group.
Round 3: everyone contributes 10. David volunteers to audit the totals.
Round 4: David's audit confirms that David, Alice, Carol, and you contributed 10, while Bob contributed 0. The project technology is unchanged.
Round 5: David again contributes 10 and publishes the ledger; Bob again contributes 0.

title: One newcomer defects while established partners remain reliable
persona: You value cooperation and avoid generalizing one person's conduct to unrelated partners.
role: You share a fishery with Alice, Bob, Carol, and newcomer David. Choose harvest from 0 to 20.
observations: Round 1: Alice, Bob, Carol, David, and you each harvest 10.
Round 2: Alice, Bob, and Carol honor 10 as they have for years; David also takes 10.
Round 3: all established partners remain at 10; David takes 18. Regeneration is normal.
Round 4: Alice, Bob, and Carol reduce to the agreed 8; David takes 20. Regeneration remains normal.
Round 5: the established partners again honor 8 and propose a sanction only for David; David takes 20 again.

title: Late generation shift after a long history containing partner disputes
persona: You value conservation and judge current evidence without letting old resolved disputes dominate.
role: Five households share a microgrid. Choose consumption from 0 to 10 units.
observations: Evening 1: generation 30; everyone consumes 5.
Evening 2: generation 30; everyone consumes 5. Alice asks a billing question that is resolved.
Evening 3: generation 30; everyone consumes 5. Bob briefly reports a faulty meter, then the utility confirms it was a display error.
Evening 4: generation 30; everyone consumes 5. Carol complains about noise; the issue is unrelated to electricity.
Evening 5: generation 30; everyone consumes 5. David pays a bill one day late and then clears it.
Evening 6: generation 30; every smart meter records consumption 5.
Evening 7: generation 30; every smart meter records consumption 5.
Evening 8: generation 30; every smart meter records consumption 5.
Evening 9: generation 30; every smart meter records consumption 5.
Evening 10: all meters still record 5, but an inverter failure reduces measured generation to 12 and the battery falls sharply.
Evening 11: the inverter remains failed, all partners reduce to 4, and generation remains 12.
